business_problem: TE Connectivity needed to help product-development teams find and reuse engineering knowledge trapped in dozens of incompatible systems without spending hours searching documents or depending on subject matter experts.
solution_summary: TE Connectivity, Capgemini, and AWS built TELme as a generative-AI research environment that turns scattered engineering knowledge into a searchable, conversational workspace. The program ingested 2.5 million documents in just over three months and was designed to scale toward 75 million documents held across 66 databases. AWS supplied the cloud infrastructure plus managed services including Amazon Bedrock and Amazon OpenSearch Service, while Capgemini used a retrieval-augmented generation architecture to combine those services with Claude 3.5 and TE's proprietary data. The result is a secure interface where engineers can search, summarize, and retrieve technical information without trawling through siloed systems or relying on subject-matter experts to answer basic questions. TELme is organized under a single API, continues to ingest more content, and is refined daily through joint feedback and governance so it can serve product-development teams at enterprise scale.

data_flow: Engineering and operational documents are ingested from dozens of databases, indexed for search and retrieval, combined with proprietary context through a RAG architecture, and surfaced through TELme so engineers can ask questions and receive summarized answers in a secure UI.
business_outcome: TE Connectivity gave engineers a secure way to search and summarize proprietary knowledge much faster, reduced time spent navigating siloed systems, and created an enterprise platform that can scale as more content is ingested.
